Subject: Recap + compliance add-ons pricing (audit logs / HSM / residency)

Hi Emma — great to meet yesterday. Thanks for walking through the HIPAA workflow and residency constraints. As promised, here’s a short recap and two ways we can structure the compliance add-ons for NY HealthSys so you can take to procurement/legal.

Context / priorities you called out:
- HIPAA coverage across PHI pipelines (analytics + inference)
- EU/US residency segregation for patient data shards (primary in us-east, backup in us-west)
- Hardware-backed key management (HSM) for production KMS
- Audit log retention and export for quarterly audits

High-level pricing constructs (ballpark for internal review only):
- Audit logs: base 30 day retention included; extended retention add-on at $0.015 per 1k events / month or a committed credit line (see attachment for tiering)
- KMS/HSM: two options — seat-based managed HSM ($1,200 / seat / mo) or usage-blend (flat service fee + per-request).
- Data residency: region surcharge 12% on token usage for dedicated residency racks; egress-free within region.

I attached a two-page options sheet and the audit-log tiering workbook to make the numbers transparent. If it helps, we can:
- Option A: seat-based HSM + 90-day audit-log credit for first year (offset to reduce initial SaaS bill)
- Option B: usage-blend HSM + residency credit applied as % rebate on committed spend for year 1

Next steps: would you prefer a single recommended path to take to procurement or both packaged side-by-side? I can also bake these into an SOW draft for legal.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise 
Redwood Inference
Attachments: NYHealthSys-Compliance-Options-2027-08-04.pdf (proposal), audit-log-pricing.xlsx (workbook)

Hi Monica — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifying questions from procurement and legal before we escalate:

1) For audit logs: can you structure a first-year credit that covers our pilot (estimated 1.8M events/month) so we don't get large burst charges during onboarding? Procurement asks for a refundable credit or an offset on committed spend.
2) HSM: law wants to see a seat-based comparison and a usage-case example with expected monthly cost for ~3 HSM-protected models (low-per-request volume but steady key rotation). Seat pricing looks attractive, but we need certainty if seat = physical HSM instance vs logical seat on a shared HSM cluster.
3) Residency credit: we are sensitive to the 12% surcharge. Would you be open to a split — 6% credit on the committed portion in year 1 and full 12% thereafter?

Also, please include a short SOW showing how audit logs will be exported for quarterly audits (format and retention assurance) — legal will not accept vague statements.

Thanks,
Emma Saini
Director, Platform Engineering
NY HealthSys

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Emma — thanks, great questions. I pulled together two clean packaging proposals (attached PDF) and a short SOW draft for the audit log export/retention piece (attached PDF + SOW draft in DocuSign link). Key points below:

Package 1 — Predictable (recommended for regulatory certainty)
- HSM: 3-seat managed HSM subscription at $1,000 / seat / month (we are offering a promotional rate vs list)
- Audit logs: 90-day retention included; extended retention to 13 months via credit model. First-year audit-log credit = $20k refundable offset applied to committed spend if onboarding volumes exceed pilot estimates.
- Residency surcharge: we can apply a 6% credit to committed spend in Year 1 (applies to baseline committed usage up to agreed cap).
- Implementation: export schema to S3/secure FTP in JSONL with signed manifests; quarterly export verification and one annual export on encrypted tape if requested.

Package 2 — Flexible (lower upfront)
- HSM: usage-blend (flat $2,500 / month service + $0.002 per KMS request) estimated at $2,900/mo for your projected load
- Audit logs: pay-as-you-go at published tiers with a 30% first-quarter onboarding credit (not refundable; applied to invoice)
- Residency: no upfront credit; reduced surcharge if committed spend grows >18% YoY.

Concession ask / proposal:
- We can offer Package 1 with a binding 9-month pilot credit ($20k) and a one-time onboarding credit to offset audit-log ingestion spikes. In return we would ask for a 12-month committed spend baseline (amount to be agreed).
- Seat price above reflects a promotional concession compared to our standard $1,200/seat.

Attached: NYHealthSys-Compliance-Options-2027-08-04.pdf (detailed numbers), audit-log-pricing.xlsx (tier workbook), nyhs-sow-draft.pdf (SOW).

If this looks good, I can:
- Convert Package 1 into an SOW + term sheet and send to Lawrence for redlines
- Schedule a short legal + procurement call early next week to close on the committed baseline and credit mechanics

Best,
Monica
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachments: NYHealthSys-Compliance-Options-2027-08-04.pdf, audit-log-pricing.xlsx, nyhs-sow-draft.pdf
